title: attribute-driven-access-catalogue-and-siem-contract
content:
Purpose:
This note captures an attribute-driven access catalogue (ADC) and a proposed SIEM export contract for RBAC v2. The goal is to unify how attributes (user, resource, environment) are modelled, how policy decisions are recorded in the audit stream, and what evidence automation needs to ingest/export for compliance review and SIEM correlation.

Audience:
- Security & compliance engineers implementing RBAC v2 telemetry
- SRE/infra for audit export and SIEM ingestion
- Platform & product for rollout gating and verification

Summary / TL;DR:
- Move from role-only assignments to an attribute-first catalogue: canonical attribute names, types, and cardinality.
- Define a minimal SIEM contract (flat JSON fields) that maps decision inputs, evaluation context, decision result, and artifacts (policy id, policy hash, model/version).
- Implement evidence hooks in the decision path so the evidence pipeline can auto-collect artifacts needed for audits (policies, prompt snapshots, rollout tags).
- Phased rollout: shadow-eval -> opt-in enforcement for teams -> org-wide enforcement with retroactive evidence backfill.

High-level design notes:
1) Attribute-driven access catalogue (ADC)
   - Canonical attributes (examples):
     * principal.id (string)
     * principal.team (string)
     * principal.isService (bool)
     * resource.type (enum: model, dataset, job, route)
     * resource.owner_team (string)
     * env.region (string)
     * request.transport (enum: api, console, internal)
     * purpose (string, free-text but indexed for common tags like: api-key-rotation, debug)
   - Each attribute entry in the catalogue: name, type, allowed_values (if enum), source (idp/profile, token, route param), example values, cardinality, and privacy classification (public/internal/secret).
   - Rationale: having a shared catalogue avoids ad-hoc attributes in policies and keeps SIEM mapping consistent.

2) Decision path and what we log (audit schema)
   - Keep audit record flat for SIEM friendliness. Each record should be a single JSON object (no nested arrays) with fixed field names so Splunk/Elastic queries are predictable.
   - Proposed mandatory fields (all flat strings unless noted):
     * event_time (ISO8601)
     * request_id
     * nexus_request_path (string) -- normalized route (e.g., /v1/generate)
     * principal_id
     * principal_type (user/service)
     * principal_team
     * resource_id
     * resource_type
     * resource_owner_team
     * action (string) -- e.g., read, write, create, delete, invoke
     * decision (allow|deny|defer|error)
     * decision_reason (short code: policy_match, no_policy, expired_cred, override)
     * policy_id (if matched)
     * policy_hash (sha256)
     * evaluation_time_ms (int as string)
     * policy_version
     * env_region
     * request_transport
     * siem_facility (string) -- internal tag for routing
     * evidence_refs (comma-separated list of artifact ids)
   - Optional fields (when available):
     * cert_fingerprint
     * session_id
     * client_ip (or obfuscated)

3) Evidence automation contract (hooks)
   - Decision engine must emit lightweight evidence references synchronously: small ids that point to a durable evidence bundle stored in evidence-store. Evidence bundle contains: full policy text, policy metadata, input attribute snapshot, policy evaluation trace (matching rules), and any user-supplied rationale/override.
   - Evidence bundle schema (stored): bundle_id, created_at, creator, attachments (policy.txt, eval_trace.json, input_snapshot.json), retention_tier. (Note: the bundle object is in object storage; audit record only carries bundle_id in evidence_refs.)
   - Evidence creation should be configurable per-route/team to avoid exponential storage growth during high-throughput endpoints; default for sensitive actions (delete model, export dataset) = immediate evidence.

4) SIEM export mapping and examples
   - Exporter respects the flat-schema; translation layers must normalize names that come from older RBAC v1 logs. Migration mapping table (examples):
     * old: user_email -> principal_id; old: role -> principal_role (still logged as hint).
     * old: resource_uri -> resource_id; normalize to short ids where possible.
   - Example event (flattened single-line JSON):
     event_time=2024-11-21T21:02:03Z request_id=REQ-abc123 nexus_request_path=/v1/models/generate principal_id=svc-inference-42 principal_type=service principal_team=platform resource_id=model-prod-llama2 resource_type=model resource_owner_team=ml action=invoke decision=allow decision_reason=policy_match policy_id=POL-998 policy_hash=sha256:... evaluation_time_ms=5 policy_version=2024-11-01 env_region=us-west-2 request_transport=api siem_facility=auth evidence_refs=BNDL-20241121-0001

Migration & rollout strategy (practical):
- Phase 0: prototype ADC and a small stateless exporter (dev cluster). Validate queries in SIEM, get SRE buy-in. (timeline: 2 weeks)
- Phase 1: shadow mode for all decisions for a single org (security team + two product teams). Produce both old and new audit records side-by-side so dashboards continue to load. (timeline: 4 weeks)
- Phase 2: gated opt-in enforcement. Teams can opt their routes into enforcement using ADC attributes. Provide migration tooling to convert existing role grants to attribute grants using heuristics and manual review. (timeline: 6–8 weeks per team)
- Phase 3: org-wide enforcement + evidence retention enabled for regulated actions. Backfill evidence for the previous 90 days for top 10 sensitive routes only. (timeline: depends on storage and infra; estimate 8 weeks)

Backwards compatibility notes:
- Keep RBAC v1 role->permission translation shim in the decision path for 6 months after enforcement to allow gradual migration. Log both role-based and attribute-based decisions with a flag that indicates which system prevailed.
- For telemetry consumers, provide a compatibility table and a short-lived pipeline that duplicates events in both old and new formats.

Operational considerations & quotas:
- Evidence bundle rate limit per org (default): 1000 bundles/min; adjustable by enterprise contract.
- Storage retention tiers: 30d (default), 365d (compliance pack), indefinite (legal hold).
- Sampling strategy: for high-throughput read-only actions, sample 0.1% of events by default and 100% for critical write/delete actions.

Validation, metrics & KPIs:
- Success criteria for rollout:
  * SIEM searches for "policy_id" must return results for 95% of audited enforcement actions after Phase 2.
  * Evidence bundle availability: 99.9% retrieval success within 2 seconds for queries from compliance team.
  * False-deny rate < 0.2% after two-week calibration per-team.
  * Migration coverage: 80% of role grants mapped to attribute rules automatically, remainder flagged for manual review.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- What attributes are allowed to be free-text vs. enumerated? Free-text increases SIEM index cost. (owner: Marcus)
- How to handle PII in attributes (e.g., user email) while keeping SIEM queries useful? Options: hash, tokenize, or keep in evidence-store only. (owner: Priya)
- Enforcement for cross-region requests: should we record both origin and evaluated-region? (owner: SRE)
- Retention default limits and cost allocation model between teams and central security.

Immediate action items (next sprint):
- Build ADC proto: YAML + CLI to register attribute entries (Ethan). JIRA: ENG-7890.
- Implement lightweight exporter that emits flat-schema events into dev SIEM (Marcus).
- Spike: evidence-store bundle prototype with minimal attachments and retrieval API (Priya).
- Create dashboards for Phase 1 shadow-mode coverage and discrepancies (Lena).

Notes to reviewers / context:
- This is intentionally pragmatic: flat schema for SIEM compatibility and an evidence-ref approach to keep production audit latency low.
- Expect follow-ups on naming conventions and attribute cardinality limits.
- We'll use the shadow phase to refine policy_hash semantics (should include policy source tree + checksum + commit id).

Appendix: quick reference commands / links:
- Git PR with proto: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbac/pull/89
- Confluence draft with full ADC table: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Attribute+Catalog+proto
- Example Jira for spike: ENG-7890

-- end --
